about: Wear OS widget design guidance from developer.android.com, for Remote Compose Wear widgets.

frames.label: Samsung
frames.description: the widget in the container Samsung's Wear launcher gives it, with semicircular ends. Content is cut only where it actually reaches into those ends; look before you judge.

frames.label: Pixel Watch
frames.description: the widget in the container the Pixel Watch launcher gives it, with rounded corners. Content is cut only where it actually reaches into those corners.

rules.guidance: Margins should be defined in percentages to avoid clipping and provide proportional scaling of elements.
rules.check: Is every piece of text, every icon and every control drawn whole, with none of its pixels missing? Answer fail only when part of a glyph, an icon or a control's own shape is visibly cut off in a picture: a letter sliced, an icon missing a side, a button's edge flattened where the edge or a container covers it. Being close to the edge, or to a curve, is not clipping, and neither is a container's own rounded outline. Look at the Samsung (round) and the Pixel Watch (squircle) pictures, answer fail only for content cut in one of them, and name which picture in your reason.

rules.guidance: Reserves at least 48.dp in size to disambiguate touch interactions if the element would measure smaller. Smaller visual sizes, such as compact and extra-small buttons, are padded out to a 48dp touch target.
rules.check: Is the tap area of every tappable control at least 48dp in each direction? Count the padding Wear adds to compact and extra-small buttons and icon buttons (their tap area is 48dp even when they draw smaller); flag only controls given a fixed size or height that leaves the tap area under 48dp.

rules.guidance: Color roles come in pairs (container and on-container) that provide a minimum of 3:1 color contrast. Custom colors should keep that contrast.
rules.check: Where the design overrides colors, does it pair each container color with its matching content (on-) role, or with colors that are clearly high contrast?

rules.guidance: All empty states should have a clear call-to-action so the user knows what to do to fix a potential issue, or find out more information.
rules.check: If this design shows an empty, error or signed-out state, does it offer a clear action? Answer not_applicable when it does not show such a state.

rules.guidance: Never hide a gesture-only action. A visible element that performs the same task must be present.
rules.check: Does every action bound to a gesture (long press, swipe, double tap) also have a visible control that performs it?

rules.guidance: Always supply your widget's background brush directly to WearWidgetDocument so the host system can paint and mask the background to the native OEM container shape. Setting a transparent or black canvas and drawing a custom rounded container inside the layout can cause floating box and letterboxing defects on some devices.
rules.check: Is the widget's background set on the root's background property (remote-m3/widget-container-small, remote-m3/widget-container-large or remote-m3/widget-container-adaptive) rather than drawn by a coloured or rounded box inside the content?

rules.guidance: Ensure your root container composable uses RemoteModifier.fillMaxSize(). Because container DP dimensions and safe insets vary across watch models, hardcoding fixed dimensions or outer padding can cause clipping or misaligned layouts.
rules.check: Does the content directly inside the widget container fill it (fillMaxSize), with no fixed width, height or outer padding?

rules.guidance: Tiles should feel focused, concise, and purpose-driven. Avoid providing a superfluous amount of functionality, and refrain from using more than one interactive component to trigger a specific action. (Tiles guidance; widgets replace Tiles.)
rules.check: Does the widget focus on one task, with no two controls doing the same thing?

rules.guidance: We don't recommend using containers for decorative or structural purposes, to avoid taps that don't do anything.
rules.check: Does every container that looks like a button (filled, rounded and button-shaped) have an action or click binding? Treat an empty or placeholder click handler as an action.

rules.guidance: Title styles are not recommended for interactive components, rather page headings or sub headings. Label styles are applied to interactive components.
rules.check: Does text inside buttons and cards use label or body styles, with title styles kept for headings outside controls? Answer not_applicable when no text style is set inside a control.

rules.guidance: Numeral text styles are used for numerical digits, usually limited to a few characters, where no localization is required.
rules.check: Is every text with a numeral style purely digits, a time or a short number (no words)? Answer not_applicable when no numeral styles are used.

rules.guidance: Tokens assign an element's type style by a configurable value, rather than a set value, making managing styles and themes considerably easier.
rules.check: Do text nodes set a style rather than fontSizeSp, lineHeightSp or letterSpacingSp, and do colours come from the theme's colour roles rather than hex values on individual components? Typography set once on the widget root (remote-m3/widget-container-small, remote-m3/widget-container-large or remote-m3/widget-container-adaptive) through its themeDisplayTypeface, themeTitleTypeface, themeBodyTypeface, themeLabelTypeface or themeTextStyle properties is the theme, and is fine.

rules.guidance: Use both icons and labels when possible. Don't rely solely on icons to prompt the user to take action.
rules.check: Are icon-only controls (icon-button, icon-only edge-button) kept to universally recognisable actions (add, close, play, settings), with other actions labelled? Answer not_applicable when there are no icon-only controls.

rules.guidance: Container roles are used as a fill color for foreground elements like buttons. They shouldn't be used for text or icons.
rules.check: Is no *Container colour role (primaryContainer, secondaryContainer, tertiaryContainer, errorContainer) used as a text colour, icon tint or contentColor? Answer not_applicable when the design names no colour roles.

rules.guidance: Because partial-height widgets integrate directly into a vertically scrolling surface, this fixed bottomSlot paradigm no longer exists, and migrating requires a deliberate UI redesign rather than a direct component swap.
rules.check: Does the widget avoid remote-m3/remote-edge-button, using an inline button or a whole-container tap instead?

rules.guidance: Rather than porting a dense, full-screen Tile layout one-to-one, streamline your design to emphasize primary information within the main content area.
rules.check: Does the widget lead with one primary piece of information rather than a dense grid of equal items?

rules.guidance: Experiences on the watch don't have the luxury of having ample space to communicate their meaning, so the most effective Tiles have easily predictable interactive components. (Tiles guidance; widgets replace Tiles.) For example, don't wrap a Play button in a tappable container showing album art: the user can't tell where the container takes them, or whether that differs from Play.
rules.check: Can a user tell from each tappable element alone what tapping it will do, and do no two overlapping tap targets lead to different outcomes (such as a clickable card or container wrapping a button that does something else)?

rules.guidance: To ensure enough space for interactive elements on smaller screens, the app title can be hidden when a Tile uses two rows (and a bottom section). This ensures the rows are tall enough (at least 48dp). (Tiles guidance; widgets replace Tiles.)
rules.check: If this design is a small widget (remote-m3/widget-container-small, 76dp tall), does it avoid stacking a title above a row of tap targets, or two rows of tap targets? Answer not_applicable for other designs.

rules.guidance: Because partial-height widgets integrate directly into a vertically scrolling surface, this fixed bottomSlot paradigm no longer exists. The same holds for the rest of a full-screen layout's watch chrome: page indicators and curved progress arcs are drawn for the round bezel of a whole screen, not for a widget in the carousel.
rules.check: Does the widget avoid full-screen watch chrome: remote-m3/remote-horizontal-page-indicator, remote-m3/remote-vertical-page-indicator and remote-m3/remote-curved-progress-indicator?

rules.guidance: Partial-height widgets integrate directly into a vertically scrolling surface, and each container has a fixed height (Small 216×76dp, Large 216×124dp). Content must fit the container rather than scroll inside it.
rules.check: Does every layout inside the widget fit within its container's fixed height, with no vertical or horizontal scroll modifier?

rules.guidance: Make the most of additional real estate by utilizing breakpoints to offer powerful new experiences on larger screens which are not possible on devices with smaller screens. An adaptive widget (remote-m3/widget-container-adaptive) resolves to the Small container (216×76dp) by dropping its supporting slot and keeping headline and action, so the supporting slot is for what the larger size adds, never for what the widget is for.
rules.check: If the root is remote-m3/widget-container-adaptive, do the headline and action slots alone still carry the widget's primary information and primary action, with the supporting slot holding only extra detail? Answer not_applicable when the root is not remote-m3/widget-container-adaptive.

rules.guidance: contentDescriptions define the text that Talkback uses to describe any content that does not have a textual representation. Avoid adding words beyond the information that is displayed.
rules.check: Does every remote-m3/remote-icon that is the whole content of a control (inside remote-m3/remote-icon-button, or a button or edge button with no text label) set a non-empty contentDescription, and does every icon beside a visible text label leave contentDescription empty so the label is not announced twice? Answer not_applicable when the design contains no remote-m3/remote-icon.
